steerable-perlin.look: 2D over a smooth angle field: swirling combed grain of even width. Hillshade reads as conifer boughs or feathers, threshold as feathered flames, the wide panel is an even feather texture with no visible grid, histogram Gaussian. FFT shows concentric rings at the octave spacing, a real banding signature of lacunarity 2. Along height contours it swirls the same way. A vortex gives concentric rings with a smooth centre, the same character as the paper's figure 2c. Ridged output gives white hair-like strands and is attractive. Weak cases: at a constant direction it is only short stretched streaks and clouds, close to what DomainAxisScale gives; without octave rotation an axis-aligned direction shows blocky stair-steps and curved lattice lines in the FFT, rotation softens the steps but the lines stay and the wide panel keeps horizontal rows; strength 0.5 is mottled with a weak direction. 3D: Sheets mode gives torn laminated slabs with a coherent direction curving through the cube, not clean shells. Fibres mode at iso 0 is close to an ordinary blobby sponge. The XZ slice panel is blotchy with only a few streaks. The 4x4 lab extension is visibly silkier and longer, flowing hair or marbled plumes. Strong warps of stretched FBm are a real rival for long lines: their laminar streamlines are longer than 2x2 grain, but stripe width varies a lot, they carry a bias from the stretch axis, go moire where strain is high, and the direction cannot be chosen.
steerable-perlin.dims: 2D and 3D measured and viewed. 3D aspect: fibres 2.1, sheets 3.3, control 1.0. 4D timing kernel only, no function or image, tiling unverified. 4x4 is 2D only.
steerable-perlin.range: -1.060..1.051 over 8 seeds at norm=1 (4 octaves, dir=1), std about 0.27. A constant near 0.92 would map it to [-1,1]; not yet applied.
steerable-perlin.node_shape: Internal octave loop. Direction X/Y/Z/W hybrids or Angle hybrid in 2D, Strength hybrid, Anisotropy Sum, Min Eigenvalue .5, Topology Fibres/Sheets, Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Octave Rotation, Output Smooth/Ridged, Window 2x2/4x4 (2D), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
steerable-perlin.port_notes: G v = e1 v + (e0-e1)(d.v) d, no matrix; v'Gv is reused for the second weight. Octaves must be internal, and the direction rotates with the lattice per octave. Contour or downslope direction needs finite differences or a surface-probe node. Not a clean-room implementation: catalogue entry and dem_steer, both shader derived, were read before the paper, nothing copied; supplemental unread. Write the port fresh from the paper and supplemental.

critic.notes: Claims reproduced: c0ratio 7.99, scalar 7.1x perlin2 at 4 octaves, aspect about 3 flat across angles, seed 7 at a 24 unit window shows the same even combed grain with no lattice, 3D sheets at seed 7 are torn laminated slabs with a coherent curving direction, fibres read as a sponge. At a constant direction it is a graph recipe: DomainRotate + DomainAxisScale(.33) + FractalFBm 4 Perlin rendered with fnlab matches the constant-angle sheet. The value is the per-lane direction hybrid, which no existing node can do, so it earns a node. Weaknesses: aspect capped near 3 by the 2x2 window, lattice envelope visible at 1 to 2 octaves (envn fixes most of it), octaves must be internal because a FractalFBm parent would sample the direction hybrid at scaled positions, 4D is 7 ns per octave by the prototyper's kernel (estimate, not re-run). AVX2 numbers were not re-measured here.
critic.improved: Added envn=1 (local envelope normalisation, one FMA per corner plus one rsqrt per octave): lattice imprint cellVarMax/Min 21x -> 2.1x at one octave and 5.3x -> 1.6x at 4 octaves, grain aspect unchanged (3.04-3.15), max slope 15 -> 37, histogram less Gaussian (kurt 2.9 -> 2.4). The 4 octave look keeps the combed grain with more even contrast and fainter FFT rings; at one octave it becomes a constant-contrast stroke field. A worthwhile option, not clearly a better default, so the gallery sheet is unchanged.

master.one_liner: Perlin noise whose grain follows a per-sample direction field, giving feathery flow-aligned texture with no lattice artifacts.
master.look: Combed, feathery streamlines: fur, feathers, wind-blown snow and sand, wood grain, muscle fibre, flowing hair, strata following a slope. With Direction taken from a height field's contours the grain wraps around hills. Prototype 5 octaves over a smooth angle field: Gaussian histogram, no grid in the wide view, clean FFT.
master.algorithm: Per lane, once per call: read direction d from hybrids (Angle in 2D or Dir X/Y/Z/W), a = |d|^2/(|d|^2+eps) fades anisotropy out where d is near zero, d = normalize(d). Metric M = e0*d*d^T + e1*(I - d*d^T), e0 = k (0.51, slow along d), e1 = (Sum-k)/(dim-1) (fast across d); this closed form replaces the shader's eigenvector code. Octave loop built into the node, same M for every octave: p = pos*freq; ip = floor(p); f = p-ip; b = 1 - S5(f) per axis, S5(t)=6t^5-15t^4+10t^3. For each of 2^d corners o: v = o-f; Mv = M*v; n = dot(g(hash(ip+o)), Mv); w = product_axis(|o_axis - b_axis|) * (1 - S5(min(|dot(v,Mv)|,1))); out += n*w. Sum octaves with Gain, then ScaleOutput. Trap: the fade weight must be |o - (1-S5(f))|. My first prototype used |o - S5(f)|, which isolates every cell into a blob with a hard visible grid.
master.why_new: Direct request: FastNoise2 discussion #159 asks for exactly this (Ideas category, links the SIGGRAPH 2025 talk). godot-proposals #1493 also names anisotropic noise in its title. FastNoise has only global stretch (DomainAxisScale) and warps. A warp shears features and pinches them; it cannot set local orientation with constant feature width. Nothing on the contact sheet looks like this.
master.simd_plan: Same 2^d corner loop as Perlin plus M*v (3 mults in 2D, 6 to 9 in 3D) and one S5 polynomial per corner; abs/min only, no branches, no atan. M computed once per lane per call. Dimension agnostic: 4 / 8 / 16 corners. Measured scalar prototype, 1 octave, including the angle field and sin/cos: 4.3x perlin2. Estimated AVX2 per octave: 2.5 / 6 / 15 ns (about 2.5x to 3x Perlin), plus direction hybrids.
master.continuity: C1 when the direction field is C1: fade weights and the metric weight both have zero first and second derivative at their ends. Measured c0ratio 8.0 at 1 octave, 7.5 at 5 octaves. A discontinuous direction input gives a C0 break in the metric, so it shows as a crease.
master.params: Feature Scale; Angle or Dir X/Y/Z/W (hybrid); Anisotropy Sum (hybrid, default 4); k (0.51); Octaves, Gain (0.67), Lacunarity built in; Output Min/Max.
master.risks: Octaves must be internal: a FractalFBm parent would sample the Direction hybrid at scaled positions, so each octave would get an unrelated field. That breaks the look, and it is why this node differs from other generators. The repo reports no licence, so implement from the paper rather than its code (I could only read the shader, the PDF could not be extracted here). Range measured about +-0.75 per octave over 8 seeds, so a measured normalising constant is needed. 4D costs 16 corners with a 4x4 metric.
master.cost_note: Estimated AVX2 per octave: 2.5 / 6 / 15 ns (about 2.5x to 3x Perlin), plus direction hybrids.

cyclic-noise.look: Better than expected up close, flawed at wide view. Large soft forms carrying long wispy wind combed smoke fibres; hillshade striking, threshold shore-like; relief shows draped ranges with sinuous combed flanks, much richer than FBm Perlin and more wind than water. FFT smooth with no rings, spokes or lattice. The raw recipe from the idea has the best close view of all but is unusable at scale: the 32 unit panel is an unmistakable knit rib, and all seeds are the same fabric with rows either vertical or horizontal. Its FFT at the default window looks clean, so the FFT alone would have missed this; long lag correlation caught it at .864-.875 against .028 for FBm Perlin. My final form adds 3 rotated layers on the lowest 2 octaves plus a one-time hash slice warp: rows are gone and r is .072, seeds now differ, but a faint wavy rhythm remains in some seeds and patches of long streaks appear where the slice shear is strong, also in the XZ slice. A weaker warp left an obvious chevron rhythm in all seeds. 3D isosurface: a big merged solid with streaked pockets and thin slits, no characteristic pore, not useful as a cave density at this window. Turbulent mode: white smoky veins with ribbed rock hillshade, range -1.36..0.74, needs its own normalisation. Against graphs at matched feature size: gradient warp plus FBm Simplex is plain cloud, plus Ridged is small cellular veins, so cyclic does read as different. The nearest rival is the shear-flow keeper, with longer swirled strokes, less large form, and it works on any source.
cyclic-noise.dims: 2D and 3D measured and viewed. 4D timing kernel only, no function or image, tiling unverified.
cyclic-noise.range: -1.056..1.083 over 8 seeds at norm=.8, std about .28-.34.
cyclic-noise.artifacts: The comparison used an earlier decor setting A4 S6
cyclic-noise.node_shape: Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Warp hybrid, Warp Growth, Base Layers, Decorrelate Amount and Scale, Mode Smooth/Turbulent, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Parabola profile only.
cyclic-noise.port_notes: c0ratio 5.5 is thin folds fooling the probe: ratios 5.98 and 7.41 at finer steps, slope 17.7, so it is continuous. The fix costs the no-hash selling point. Golden frequencies, more warp and per-octave bases left r at .63-.88; only the slice warp removed the periodicity. Open choice: keep as a node, or a source-free preset of shear-flow.

critic.notes: Checks reproduce (range -1.06..1.08, scalar 4.06x perlin2, c0 probe 5.5 from sharp folds with finer-step ratios 6-7.4). The close view and the relief are the strongest images of the family after steerable: silky wind-combed fibres on large forms. But at seed 7 window 32 the whole field is sheared along one diagonal, upper left to lower right, in the gray, the hillshade and the XZ slice, and the same orientation appears at every decorS tested: the slice decorrelation axes are fixed oblique directions, so the final form trades the knit rows of the raw recipe for a global shear direction that all seeds share. The raw recipe is an unmistakable knit rib at 24 to 32 units. Compared with existing graphs: gradient warp + FBm is plain cloud, and Warp Fractal Progressive on the existing sheet gives wispy marbling of a similar family without the shear bias; the shear-flow lab keeper is the nearest look and takes any source. The no-hash selling point is gone once the slice warp is needed. Keep as a showcase preset or an example of a source-free fibre field, not as a general node.
critic.improved: Tried decorS 6, 9, 14 at seed 7 window 32: all three keep the same diagonal shear bands, 14 only slightly weaker, so nothing changed in the gallery.

tournament.notes: Checks reproduce (range -1.06..1.08, 4.06x perlin2 scalar, c0 probe 5.5 from sharp folds). Close view and relief are attractive silky wind-combed fibres. But at seed 7 window 32 the whole field is sheared along one diagonal in gray, hillshade and XZ slice, and the orientation is the same at every decorS because the slice axes are fixed, so all seeds share a fabric direction; the raw recipe is a knit rib. Warp Fractal Progressive on the existing sheet and the shear-flow keeper are the same family. The no-hash selling point is gone once the slice warp is needed. Showcase preset, not a general node.

Raw recipe parabola 7.29 / 7.29 / 9.52, sine 12.59 / 12.56 / 14.74. The idea's 0.7x Perlin per octave is wrong for true sine: about 1.4-2.3x. Parabola about 0.8-1.4x.

artist-terrain.note: Close relief is silky wind-combed ranges; seed 7 w32 shows one diagonal shear across the whole field and all seeds share the fabric direction.

artist-material.note: Silky wind-combed close up, but the critic's wide view shows everything sheared along one diagonal.

voxel-engineer.note: Silky relief, but one fixed diagonal fabric across seeds rules out general use.

maintainer.note: Attractive silky combed fibres close up; the wide view is a knit rib sheared along one diagonal on every seed.

graphics-researcher.note: The nimitz shadertoy recipe: silky combed relief, but every seed shares a fabric direction and the wide view is a knit rib. Decorrelation helps, does not cure.

creative.note: Silky clouds and pleasant relief. The volume shows flat axis-aligned streaks.

master.one_liner: Lattice-free fractal of sin(dot(cos(p), sin(p.zxy))) terms with a per-octave orthonormal rotation, lacunarity and sine domain warp (nimitz/Wrighter/0b5vr 'cyclic noise'): fibrous, marbled, flowing structure in 2D/3D at pure-ALU cost.
master.look:
Organic, fibrous, flowing filaments and marble-like veins with no lattice at all; at low octaves large smooth 'plasma', at higher octaves tangled fibre networks; turbulent mode gives cellular-ish rope structure. Visually unlike Perlin/Simplex (which have isotropic blobs) and unlike Cellular.
[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Soft billowy/foamy structure with faint wave-like anisotropy, cloudy when summed; cyclic (Warp>0) version swirls like protean clouds; triangle profile gives crumpled paper. Reads as fbm from a distance but with a wavier, more organic micro-structure. Not on the sheet (SineWave is a single axis-aligned wave).
master.algorithm:
Params: Octaves N (int, 4-8), Gain (0.6), Lacunarity (1.5), Warp (hybrid, 0.3), WarpFreq (1.2), WarpGrowth (1.5), SeedDirection (from seed: hashed unit vector).
Setup: rot = orthoBasis(seedDir) (3x3 rotation whose z axis = seedDir; 2D: a 2x2 rotation by a hashed angle plus a third coordinate = seed constant; 4D: a hashed 4x4 rotation = product of two plane rotations).
Gen(p): p3 = (x,y,z) (2D: z = seed-derived constant); amp=1; wf=WarpFreq; sum=0; norm=0; for i<N: p3 += sin(p3.zxy * wf - 2*wf) * Warp; sum += sin(dot(cos(p3), sin(p3.zxy))) * amp; norm += amp; p3 = (rot * p3) * Lacunarity; wf *= WarpGrowth; amp *= Gain. Output sum/norm (measured: multiply by ~1.3 for [-1,1] coverage); Turbulent mode: 1 - 2*|sum|/norm.
0b5vr variant (vector-valued, fits DomainWarp): accumulate cross(cos(p3), sin(p3.zxy)) as a warp vector.
Seed sensitivity: the seed enters through the rotation basis and the constant offset; per-octave re-rotation by hashed bases (seed, i) gives more variety.

[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Precompute per octave k (when params set): rotation matrix R_k = GoldenRotation^k (2D: rotate by 137.5 deg; 3D: rotation of 137.5 deg about axis (1, phi, phi^2) normalised; 4D: product of two plane rotations by 137.5 deg and 137.5*phi deg), scale s_k = Lacunarity^k, amplitude a_k = Gain^k.
q = p * Frequency; acc = 0; norm = 0
for k in 0..Octaves-1:
  q = R_k * q * (k==0 ? 1 : Lacunarity)
  if Warp > 0: q += Warp * sin(q.yzx)              // nimitz cyclic noise: the domain is bent by its own sines; 2D: q += Warp*sin(q.yx)
  v = sum over axes i of cos(q_i) * sin(Phi * q_{(i+1) mod dim})   // 2D: cos x sin(phi y) + cos y sin(phi x); Phi = golden ratio keeps it non-periodic
  Profile enum: Sine as above; Triangle: replace cos/sin by tri(x)=4*|fract(x/2pi)-0.5|-1 (nimitz triNoise: cheaper, C0 creased); Ridged: v = 1 - |v|/dim
  acc += a_k * v ; norm += a_k * dim
out = acc / norm (then measured scale: the dim-term sum rarely reaches +-dim, multiply by ~1.6)
Seed: add a seed-derived phase offset per axis (q += seedPhase) so seeds give different fields (no hash anywhere).
master.why_new: No lattice, no hash per sample, native 3D with trivial 2D/4D, and a signature look prized in the demoscene; also cheap (N octaves of 3 sin + 3 cos + a dot). Could not be built from existing nodes except by an unwieldy chain of SineWave + DomainRotate + warps.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free, fixed octave loop, no memory. Per octave: dim matrix mults (dim^2 FMA) + dim SinCos (~25 ops each) -> 2D ~ 60 ops/octave (~0.7x Perlin 2D), 3D ~ 100 ops (~0.5x Perlin 3D), 4D ~ 140 ops (~0.4x Perlin 4D). Triangle profile ~3x cheaper. Dimension-agnostic GenT with precomputed matrices.
master.params: Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Warp (hybrid), WarpFreq, WarpGrowth, Mode enum {Smooth, Turbulent}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Looks bad at high frequencies / few octaves (periodic sin structure shows, as SquidSquad's docs note); normalisation is empirical; seeds give limited structural variety unless per-octave bases are hashed.
[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Visible large-scale banding in huge flat views (Xor notes 'patterns in large flat scenes'); anisotropy at octave 1 (needs >=3 octaves to look isotropic). Range normalisation must be measured. Seeds only shift phases, so different seeds are translations of the same field unless rotation angles are also seed-perturbed (do that: angle += small seed-derived irrational offset).
master.cost_note: Per octave: dim matrix mults (dim^2 FMA) + dim SinCos (~25 ops each) -> 2D ~ 60 ops/octave (~0.7x Perlin 2D), 3D ~ 100 ops (~0.5x Perlin 3D), 4D ~ 140 ops (~0.4x Perlin 4D).
master.variant_notes: Xor's gyroid dot noise is the same family: hash-free octaves of products of sines under irrational rotation, plus self-warp.

queue.name: CyclicNoise
queue.reason: Lattice-free fibrous marble with flat cost across dimensions, a common shader recipe missing here. Seeds look related and it is weak at few octaves.

wave-noise-sliced.look: Keeper for its narrow band outputs, not as a general spectral noise. Real, N=8: soft single scale blobs, threshold a clean worm labyrinth, wide panel an even dot and worm texture with no lattice. In gray at a glance this is close to Perlin or SuperSimplex; the value is elsewhere. Wired (spike profile, N=16): crossing tapered straight needles, wide panel straw or felt, 3D thin flat crossing blades. The strongest new look, and nothing on the existing sheet resembles it. Ridged: thin closed-loop net of one cell size; 3D iso .5 gives thin curved membrane walls joined into an open foam, the best 3D result of the family; its relief is a knife edge maze with deep pits, regular and artificial. Width dial (N=16, tilt .15): 180 labyrinth, 90 wavy labyrinth, 45 wavy ripples with dislocations, 20 near straight stripes with amplitude beats, hillshade like sand ripples; 3D width 40 gives thick parallel plates with holes and bridges. Against lattice-phasor the role overlaps but the look differs: wave is soft and seamless, phasor is hard contrast zebra with straight kernel seams. The plain Real 3D sponge is nearly interchangeable with the warped TPMS keeper. Constant contrast fringes are only blobby with phase pinch points at this N, not long phasor stripes. Failures: harmonics and power law (see wave-noise); broad band with few directions shows long straight wave lines (N=8 obvious, N=16 faint, N=32 clean), matching the deck's 4 / 30 / 60 direction picture. FFT: plain N=16 is a thin ring of 32 discrete dots. Phase-only slices stay as spokes, wave vectors still discrete. Tilted slices fill it into a solid ring with faint concentric side rings. The default N=8 still shows strong spokes in log scale.
wave-noise-sliced.dims: 2D and 3D measured and viewed. 4D timing kernel only, no function or image, tiling unverified. Measured flat cost: +3.7 percent 2D to 4D.
wave-noise-sliced.range: Real -1.303..1.293 over 8 seeds at norm=.33, so the constant should be nearer .25. Ridged measured down to -5.76, the normaliser is wrong and needs fixing. Wired clamps to [-1,1] with mean about -0.52, mostly black by design.
wave-noise-sliced.node_shape: Directions N, Frequency, Output Real/Ridged/Wired/Magnitude/Fringes, Spike Sharpness, Anisotropy Angle and Width (floats, table time), Slice Size, Slice Tilt, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. No harmonics, no profile table. Optional 2D Direction Lattice mode with Angle hybrid.
wave-noise-sliced.port_notes: Use a carrier polynomial: AVX2 gathers cost 26.68 ns for 16 complex profiles against 7.00 for sincos. Peak long-lag correlation N=16: plain .797, phase slices .220, global warp .292, tilted slices .039-.044, FBm Perlin .028. Tilt is my reading of deck slide 15, without per-slice position jitter; TOG paper unread. Denormal trap measured: spike as v^128 costs 38.22 ns at N=16, compact crest (1-k(1-v))^4 costs 15.05 with the same look. Alternate the sign of d in the table, or Magnitude and Speckle streak. Seeds change phases and slice hashes only.

critic.params: Real: N=16,S=3,sj=0.5,prof=1,aoff=0.5 (N=8 shows direction chains). Wired: N=16,S=3,sj=0.4,prof=1,f=0.5,spike=7,aoff=0.5. Stripes: N=16,S=3,sj=0.15,prof=1,f=1.5,angle=30,width=30.
critic.notes: Checks reproduce (c0 8.02, scalar 2.36x perlin2 at N=8, range -1.30..1.29 at norm .33). The default N=8 Real is not clean: at seed 7 window 24 to 32 the blobs line up in straight chains along the 8 wave directions, in 2D and in the XZ slice; N=12 is fainter, N=16 reads isotropic. So the honest cost of a clean Real output is N=16 sliced, 12.5-15 ns in the prototyper's AVX2 table, about 9-11x real Perlin in 2D, not the 5-8x quoted for N=8. Real at a glance is Perlin with a narrower band; Ridged is the same closed-loop net and the same 3D membrane foam as FractalRidged(Octaves=1, Source=Simplex) at iso .5, rendered with fnlab, so it is not the best 3D result of the family, it is an existing graph. What is new: Wired needles (crossing straight tapered lines, 3D crossing blades; nothing in the catalogue does this), the width dial from labyrinth to seamless dislocated stripes, and the 3D parallel slabs. Those are striking but niche and 8-15 ns, hence showcase. Ridged normaliser is wrong (measured down to -5.76 in the prototyper's grid). Wave vol at seed 7 N=8 is a clean sponge, confirmed.
critic.improved: aoff=0.5 (half step offset of the direction table): wave 0 was exactly axis aligned and the Wired output drew it as one long bright horizontal row across the field at seed 7 window 32; with the offset no wave is within 4 degrees of an axis and the row is gone.

master.one_liner: Sum of N randomly oriented hyperplanar waves with random phases, each wave a precomputed/analytic 1D band-limited profile; gives exact spectral control, isotropy or anisotropy, Gaussian or phasor/ridged outputs, in any dimension at near-Perlin cost (Guehl et al. SIGGRAPH 2025; LRP noise Gilet 2014).
master.look: Smooth band-limited isotropic noise with no lattice artefacts (clean ring spectrum), or with narrow AnisoWidth: fibres, brushed/streaked materials, marble veins; Phase output gives phasor-like stripes; narrow band + Ridged gives 'wired/crystal' nets (paper). Visually cleaner and more controllable than FBm Simplex, and different from everything on the sheet in the FFT (ring instead of blob).
master.algorithm:
Params: Directions N (int, 8-32), FreqMin, FreqMax (floats, band), Harmonics M (int 2-6), AnisoAngle (hybrid), AnisoWidth (hybrid, pi = isotropic), SliceSize S (float), Output enum {Real, Phase, Magnitude, Ridged=1-|Real|}.
Setup when params change (small per-node tables are allowed): for i<N: direction d_i stratified over the circle (2D) / sphere via Fibonacci spiral (3D) / 4-sphere (4D), centred on AnisoAngle with spread AnisoWidth; for m<M: frequency f_m log-spaced in [FreqMin,FreqMax], amplitude A_m from the desired spectrum (e.g. 1/f^beta), phase phi_im = rnd(seed,i,m)*2pi.
Gen(p): Re=Im=0; for i<N: t = dot(p, d_i); // alignment-artefact reduction from the paper: slice the axis into cells of width S, jitter per slice: k = floor(t/S + jitter_i), u = frac; use a per-slice phase offset dphi = rnd(hash(seed,i,k))*2pi and blend with the neighbouring slice: w = smoothstep(u) ; for m<M: a = 2pi f_m t; Re += A_m*( (1-w)*cos(a+phi_im+dphi_k) + w*cos(a+phi_im+dphi_{k+1}) ); Im same with sin. Output Real = Re/sqrt(N*sum A_m^2/2) (analytic Gaussian normalisation), Phase = atan2(Im,Re)/pi (phasor-like stripes), Magnitude, Ridged.
Without slicing (S=inf) it is a pure sum of plane waves, exactly LRP-style spectral noise, cheaper but with visible long-range wave alignment; S ~ 2-4 wavelengths removes it.
master.why_new: FastNoise has no node with explicit spectral control (band-pass, slope, anisotropy); fractal sums only approximate 1/f. Wave noise gives exact band-pass and anisotropy in 2/3/4D at the cost of N*M sincos, and the same node also produces phasor-style and ridged non-Gaussian outputs. It also animates well via a phase/time hybrid.
master.simd_plan: Fully branch-free: N x M fixed loop of FMAs + Sin/Cos (FS::Sin/Cos are polynomial, ~10 ops each). N=16, M=3: 48 sincos ~ 4-6x Perlin in 2D, and the cost is dimension-independent (only the dot product grows) which makes 3D/4D cheaper than Simplex3D/4D relative to quality. Directions/amplitudes live in a per-node table (<1 KB).
master.continuity: C-infinity (sums of sinusoids with smooth slice blending). Phase output has isolated singularities like PhasorNoise.
master.params: Directions N (int), Harmonics M (int), FreqMin/FreqMax (float), SpectralSlope (float), AnisoAngle (hybrid), AnisoWidth (hybrid), SliceSize (float), Phase/Time (hybrid), Output (enum), Feature Scale.
master.risks: Too few directions shows plane-wave alignment (paper: 30-60 for perfect isotropy, 8-16 is fine at fractal scale). Normalisation of non-Gaussian outputs is empirical. Per-lane hybrid AnisoAngle requires rotating the direction table per lane (2D: one sincos per direction, acceptable).
master.cost_note: N=16, M=3: 48 sincos ~ 4-6x Perlin in 2D, and the cost is dimension-independent (only the dot product grows) which makes 3D/4D cheaper than Simplex3D/4D relative to quality.

wave-noise.look: Same kernel as wave-noise-sliced, so it needs no node of its own. Its reason to exist was harmonics and power law spectra, and those did not earn a mode. M=3 log spaced tilted waves: cloud scale blobs with an even fish scale ripple over everything in the hillshade, frayed threshold, FFT a target of rings and spokes. A scaly texture, not an FBm replacement. Power law with one frequency per direction, N=32 tilted: ordinary soft lumpy noise with a starburst FFT, nothing FBm lacks. Table profile band .5-4 at N=16: an exact band edge in the FFT, but straight spokes of discrete directions, and a look close to plain noise.

master.one_liner: Sum of M random-direction plane waves with controlled spectrum (Berry monochromatic ring, Kolmogorov/Weierstrass power law, or N-fold quasicrystal), with Real, Speckle and Phase outputs.
master.look:
Ring: band-limited isotropic 'monochromatic' blobs and stripes whose zero set is Berry nodal domains (percolation-like labyrinth), unlike Perlin's mixed scales. PowerLaw: isotropic 1/f^beta noise without any lattice signature in the FFT. Speckle: laser-speckle granules with sharp dark zeros (phase vortices) and bright hot spots. PhaseSin: equal-contrast interference fringes with dislocations. Symmetric 5/7/12: quasicrystal rosettes. Good for Turing patterns (animal coats, coral, sand ripples), clouds with set spectral slope, speckle/dust masks, interference art, optical textures.
[WaveShell, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped. 3D isosurface, 6 waves: aperiodic sponge with visibly ordered rows and local five-fold motifs that never repeat. 24 waves: amorphous bicontinuous spinodal sponge with one characteristic pore size, like aerogel, polymer blends or Nuclepore. Both phases percolate at threshold 0. 2D grey slice is soft and blobby and on its own not distinctive, so the value is in 3D, FFT ring and isotropy. Good for sponges, porous rock, sci-fi lattices, labyrinth masks.
master.algorithm:
Setup (constant tables, no per-lane state): a low-discrepancy direction table D[0..M-1] (2D: angles pi*i/M + golden jitter; 3D: Fibonacci sphere; 4D: Fibonacci on S^3), and a stratified table t_i = (i+0.5)/M.
Gen(seed, x):
  // decorrelate seeds with ONE random rotation of the sample point instead of M rotations of the directions
  R = rotation from hash(seed): 2D one angle (1 sincos); 3D random quaternion from 3 hash floats (Shoemake, 2 sincos + 2 sqrt); 4D two angles in two planes.
  x' = R * x * k0                  (k0 from Feature Scale)
  re = 0; im = 0; norm = 0
  for i in 0..M-1 (fixed count):
    phi_i = 2pi * hash01(seed, i)                       // integer hash, cheap
    Spectrum == Ring:      k_i = 1,  a_i = 1
    Spectrum == PowerLaw:  k_i = 2^(Bandwidth * frac(t_i + hash01(seed,i+M)*0.5)) ; a_i = k_i^(-Beta/2)
    Spectrum == Symmetric: direction = fixed (cos(pi i/M), sin(pi i/M)), no rotation, phi_i = 0 or random
    theta = k_i * dot(D[i], x') + phi_i
    s = Sin(theta); c = Cos(theta) (c only needed for Speckle/Phase)
    re += a_i * c; im += a_i * s; norm += a_i*a_i
  g = 1/Sqrt(norm/2)                                     // unit variance
  Output == Real:    v = im * g * 0.33 ; if Sharpness>0: v = tanh(Sharpness*v)/tanh(Sharpness) (tanh via Exp)
  Output == Speckle: I = (re*re + im*im)/norm ; v = 1 - 2*Exp(-I)          // |psi|^2 is exponential-distributed -> uniform in [-1,1]
  Output == PhaseSin: v = (re*cosPsi + im*sinPsi) * InvSqrt(re*re+im*im+eps)  // cos(phase - Psi): unit-contrast fringes, no atan2 needed
  Output == Phase:   v = atan2poly(im, re)/pi                                // sawtooth, discontinuous
Turing/Swift-Hohenberg look: Ring + Sharpness ~3 gives labyrinth stripes of exact wavelength 2pi/k0; add a Bias before tanh to switch stripes->spots; Symmetric M=3 gives hexagonal spot lattice.
Weierstrass-Mandelbrot: PowerLaw with k_i on a geometric ladder gamma^n and a_i = gamma^((D-3)n) is exactly the Ausloos-Berman 2D W-M function.
master.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet is band-limited or has a controllable spectrum: FBm only reaches octave-spaced power laws and always inherits lattice artefacts. WaveNoise has no lattice window at all (so no seams, no 4D blow-up: cost is nearly flat across 2D/3D/4D), gives exact ring spectra (the Turing/Chladni/Berry family), speckle statistics, and subsumes the Weierstrass-Mandelbrot terrain function and quasicrystal interference as parameter settings.
master.simd_plan: Fully branch-free: fixed M loop, all per-wave constants from tables + integer hash. Per wave: 1 dot (d FMAs), 1 hash, 1 Sin (+1 Cos for complex outputs). No lattice window. Per-lane seed handled by rotating x once per lane. Est. AVX2 cost M=16: 2D ~2.5-3x Perlin, 3D ~1.3x Perlin3D, 4D ~0.8x Perlin4D (dimension only adds one FMA per wave). Far-coordinate precision: reduce theta mod 2pi before Sin (Round(theta*inv2pi) FMA) since |x|*k0 grows. GenT<P...> parameter pack works directly; tiling via GenTileable2D works since the function is defined for any 4D point.
master.continuity: C-infinity for Real, Speckle, PhaseSin (except isolated zeros of psi where PhaseSin is undefined; masked to 0). Phase (sawtooth) is discontinuous across the branch cut by design.
master.params: Waves M (int 4-64), Spectrum enum {Ring, PowerLaw, Symmetric}, Feature Scale (k0), Bandwidth octaves (float, PowerLaw), Beta spectral slope (float, 5/3 Kolmogorov in 1D-energy convention; document the power-vs-amplitude factor 2), Output enum {Real, Speckle, PhaseSin, Phase}, Sharpness (hybrid: tanh gain; spatially varying sharpness turns smooth noise into Turing stripes locally), Bias (hybrid: stripes vs spots), Phase offset Psi (hybrid, animates fringes), Seed.
master.risks:
Small M (<8) shows visible beating and long-range interference; Ring covariance J0(kr) has oscillating long tails (that is the physics, but users may read it as repetition). Statistical stationarity only: one seed is one global realisation, locally it still looks uniform. Normalisation of Real by 0.33*sigma clips Gaussian tails ~0.3% of samples. 4D Fibonacci-on-S^3 table needs care to be uniform.
[WaveField, lattice-kernels] Low K shows periodic beat and repetition at large scale; K>=16 needed. Phase precision degrades at huge coordinates because f*dot grows; wrap needed. Homogeneous everywhere, so it is a texture rather than a terrain basis. Hybrid frequency impossible in plane-wave form.
[FourierNoise, terrain-tools-engines] Not local: with N < 12 individual plane waves are visible as banding; statistics are stationary but the pattern is quasi-periodic at very large scales (recurrences when few incommensurate frequencies); seed changes phases/rotation only, so different seeds share a 'family' spectrum (acceptable since the spectrum is the parameter).
sources: M. V. Berry, 'Regular and irregular semiclassical wavefunctions', J. Phys. A 1977 (random wave model; recalled, not fetched)
master.cost_note: AVX2 cost M=16: 2D ~2.5-3x Perlin, 3D ~1.3x Perlin3D, 4D ~0.8x Perlin4D (dimension only adds one FMA per wave).
master.variant_notes: Global sum of N plane waves with a designed spectrum. Features folded in: exact tiling by snapping wave vectors to integer periods (FourierNoise); a Crystallinity hybrid sliding from icosahedral quasicrystal to amorphous spinodal in 3D (WaveShell); threshold-to-labyrinth use (RingSpectrumNoise); J0 ring kernels as the fallback when wavelength must vary in space (WaveField).
